title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1LC1RA_1RA1LD_0LC0LA_0RE1RF_0RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1LC1RA_1RA1LD_0LC0LA_0RE1RF_0RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Like 1RB---_0RC0RD_1LD1RB_0LE0LC_1RA0LF_1LD1LE in this group, its tape has two parts: a stretch 1 0 1 0 … and a solid block of 1s. At the left end the stretch is on the left (0 0 0 (10)^909 1^1859); at the right end the block is on the left (0 1^238 (10)^1718). Unlike in that machine, the block does not keep its length across a trip.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps; the C simulator shows none in 109. How the sizes change is not yet understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,680 cells have been visited and 3,050 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Tape shape
claims.text: At every side switch printed near 109 steps the tape is two parts: at the left end 0 0 (10)^r 1^m or 0 1 1 (10)^r 1^m (r, m = 1052, 1564 at step 989,218,161; 213, 3249 at step 996,727,782), at the right end 0 1^m (10)^r 0 (m, r = 1437, 1103 at step 972,250,598; 238, 1717 at step 996,613,780). Consecutive sizes are erratic (m at the right: 3627, 238 after left-end m = 9, 1564).

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.341). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345).

claims.title: Growth like t<sup>1/3</sup>
claims.text: After step 5·10<sup>8</sup>: 127 side switches, 3,929,109 steps apart on average (≈ 0.291·w<sup>2</sup>, w = 3679), about 6.0 cells of width per switch; fitted width exponent 0.344 after step 10<sup>7</sup>.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The halting transition is F reading 1. F is entered only from E reading 1 (moving right). So a halt is exactly E>1 1: E on a 1 with a 1 to its right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The two-part shape holds at the switches printed; the map from one pair of sizes to the next, and why E never reads two adjacent 1s, are open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is an alternating stretch next to a solid block of 1s, and the two swap sides on every trip; a trip costs about the width squared, for several cells of growth, so the width grows like the cube root of the time.

facts.text: Width of the tape at its last extension before step 10<sup>9</sup>.
Side switches in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps.

sections.heading: A stretch and a block that swap sides
html: The tape at the last side switches:
The parts swap sides on every trip, but their sizes change: no rule yet.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: The head goes back and forth across the whole tape. After step 5·108 there are 127 side switches (extensions of the tape on the other side from the last one), on average 3,929,109 steps apart, which is about 0.291·w2 for the final width w = 3679; each adds about 6.0 cells to the width. A constant gain per w2 steps gives w3 ~ t. The fitted exponent of the width after step 107 is 0.344.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.341). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,680 cells (1,766 left of the start, 1,213 right), with a density of 1s of 0.829.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: solid block and alternating stretch, erratic sizes
summary: The tape is an alternating stretch and a solid block of 1s, alternating on the left and solid on the right at the left end, the other way round at the right end; the sizes change erratically. Width ~ t^(1/3).
